subtitle: All the news that's fit to Fingerprint

lead.headline: Netflix Opens Its Ad Tier to Trade Desk Audience Data
lead.dek: Advertisers buying Netflix through Kokai can target with first-party lists and third-party segments from November.
lead.body: Starting in November, advertisers buying Netflix through The Trade Desk's Kokai can target with their own first-party lists and with third-party segments from a marketplace of more than 4 million segments across more than 300 providers. The Trade Desk joins Yahoo DSP and Amazon DSP as a route for audience data onto Netflix inventory. Until now, Trade Desk buyers could use only Netflix's own targeting on Netflix inventory. The Trade Desk says in-DSP measurement is “coming soon” with no date given. It matters because it removes a constraint on one of the largest premium SVOD ad supplies in programmatic.

stories.headline: Netflix Trims 2026 Ad Revenue Forecast to $2.7 Billion
stories.dek: Partner integrations slipped, and co-CEO Greg Peters says the ads business is behind its target.
stories.body: In third-quarter results released October 20, Netflix cut its 2026 advertising revenue expectation to about $2.7 billion from roughly $3 billion, citing a slower rollout of some ad product capabilities and partner integrations. Co-CEO Greg Peters said getting integrations with partners to the model Netflix wants takes more work, and shares fell about 6% after hours. For programmatic buyers, the pace of Netflix's partner-DSP ramp will set how fast its ad inventory scales.

stories.headline: Comscore's First Score Report Puts Streaming at 22% of TV Ad Exposure
stories.dek: YouTube and Tubi lead the streamers, but broadcast still holds the largest share of time.
stories.body: Comscore's first Score Report, covering August 2026, put broadcast at 43.2% of measured TV ad exposure time, cable at 34.5% and streaming at 22.3%, up from 16.1% a year earlier. Among streamers, YouTube excluding YouTube TV held 44% of ad exposure time and Tubi 12%. The metric counts only ads seen on in-home TV devices and is built on Comscore's TV measurement and automatic content recognition data. It gives buyers a third-party exposure yardstick for weighing streaming budgets against linear.

stories.headline: Netflix Adds Its Own Pixel and Widens the Conversion API
stories.dek: More than 20 lower-funnel events now feed one standardized measurement layer inside Netflix's Ads Suite.
stories.body: Netflix unveiled the Netflix Pixel and an expanded Conversion API covering more than 20 lower-funnel events, standardizing conversion and brand-lift measurement inside its Ads Suite. Advertisers can build audiences from their own conversion data. Outcome-based targeting and measurement on premium streaming inventory is now reaching the programmatic buying layer, not staying inside Netflix's direct channels. It matters because outcome measurement is becoming the price of admission for SVOD budgets.

stories.headline: LinkedIn B2B Audiences Now Buyable on CTV Through Google DV360
stories.body: As of October 22, advertisers can target LinkedIn audiences by job title, industry and company size when buying LinkedIn CTV inventory through Google's DV360. VistaPrint tested the offering over a campaign that ended in September, and LinkedIn claims 2.6 times stronger awareness lift for B2B audiences than other providers. LinkedIn says 94% of its members watch some ad-supported CTV. It matters because it adds a third major DSP route to LinkedIn CTV, widening professional-audience buying inside a platform many agencies already run.

stories.headline: Brazil's Paid-Ad Rules Take First Effect October 23
stories.dek: Joint rules on paid advertising and content amplification reach internet application providers.
stories.body: Joint rules from Brazil's consumer, digital rights and digital policy secretariats govern paid advertising and content amplification by internet application providers, with first provisions in force October 23. Coverage says the rules apply to providers with more than one million monthly active users in Brazil and require a free, public, searchable ad repository kept for at least a year, plus verification duties for financial-product ads. Secondary summaries disagree on the ordinance number and some dates, so the official text should be checked before phased obligations are cited. It matters because it pushes Brazilian platform ad transparency toward the repository model already set by the EU Digital Services Act.

stories.headline: Netflix Ad Tier Reaches 14 Million UK Viewers, Barb Data Shows
stories.dek: Filed after the first UK upfront; the ad-supported plan expands to nine more European markets next March.
stories.body: At its first UK upfront on 24 September, Netflix said its ad-supported plan reaches more than 14 million UK viewers, citing Barb data. The same release says the ad tier will launch on 1 March 2027 in Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Ireland, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Sweden and Switzerland. For UK buyers the reach figure sets the scale of the premium SVOD pool that programmatic access will eventually draw on.

stories.headline: IPL 2026 Reach Tops 1.2 Billion as Connected TV Grows 22%
stories.dek: Filed in June; the freshest verified India CTV audience data this edition.
stories.body: JioStar reported combined IPL 2026 reach of over 1.2 billion across TV and digital, up 7 per cent year on year, with connected-TV reach up 22 per cent. The company said 22 sponsors partnered with JioHotstar on digital and 16 joined Star Sports on linear, with 125 more advertisers than the prior season. No 2026 ad revenue total was disclosed. It matters because mass sports audiences are moving onto the connected-TV screen at scale in India.

stories.headline: Mercado Ads Adds Netflix Inventory in Brazil and Mexico for 2027
stories.dek: Commerce-media buyers get purchase-data matching on Netflix's ad tier in the region's two largest streaming-ad markets.
stories.body: Mercado Ads, the ad unit of Mercado Livre, will sell Netflix Ads inventory in Brazil and Mexico through its programmatic network, unveiled at its Break The Tape upfront in São Paulo in late September. Advertisers can define audiences using Mercado Livre's buyer data across about 131 million annual buyers and tie exposure to marketplace purchases. Netflix's ad tier has over 35 million monthly viewers in Brazil and over 29 million in Mexico. The integration takes effect in 2027, with expansion to other Latin American markets dependent on Netflix. It matters because it gives commerce-media buyers a closed-loop measurement route into a major SVOD ad tier.

stories.headline: Bell Media Ad Revenue Rises 5.3% on World Cup Demand
stories.dek: Filed in August; digital video and live sports carried the quarter while traditional ad demand softened.
stories.body: Bell Media's advertising revenue rose 5.3 per cent year on year in the second quarter of 2026, driven by FIFA World Cup demand and higher digital video ad revenue, while traditional ad demand softened. The World Cup reached 30.5 million Canadians across TSN, RDS, CTV, Noovo and Crave, and Crave subscriptions rose 23 per cent to 5.07 million. Operating costs rose 10.9 per cent, pulling the adjusted EBITDA margin down to 26.6 per cent from 27.9 per cent. It matters because live sports on CTV and Crave is the main growth lever for Canadian CTV sellers.

stories.headline: Nexxen Opens TCL and Hisense Home Screens to Programmatic Buyers
stories.dek: Filed in June; the most recent verified China-brand smart-TV ad development.
stories.body: V, formerly VIDAA, said on 3 June that advertisers can run programmatic live-sports campaigns on Hisense and Toshiba smart TVs through Nexxen's DSP or SSP, with native home-screen placements shown at power-on. In May, Nexxen said TCL's native home-screen inventory is now programmatically accessible globally. Nexxen reported Q1 2026 CTV revenue of $29.4 million, up 12 per cent. It matters because OEM home screens from Chinese-owned TV brands are becoming programmatic supply for global buyers.

stories.headline: The Receipt Is the Medium
stories.dek: Netflix's new pixel does not change what is on the screen. It changes what the screen is for.
stories.body:
Television was once a window onto a shared event. This month Netflix added its own pixel and widened its conversion interface to more than twenty lower-funnel events, and the trade press filed it under measurement. That is the usual mistake. The programme has not changed. The form has: the evening's story now carries a till inside it, and the viewer becomes a receipt that arrives later, in someone else's report.

Every medium extends one faculty and amputates another. The ledger extends the sale across the living room; it amputates the moment of looking. Comscore's first Score Report puts streaming at 22.3 per cent of measured TV ad exposure time, broadcast at 43.2 and cable at 34.5. Streaming holds a minority of the eye and a growing share of the counter. Put them side by side and the old ratio reverses: the set is hot for the marketer, who sees the sale, and cool for the viewer, who has no idea the pixel is there. Ask what the set is doing and the honest answer is no longer the programme. The old balance between seeing and hearing has tilted toward the hand that clicks.

The advertiser sees the sale before the sitting is over. The viewer goes on following the story, and the story goes on being the figure nobody looks at. Nothing in the ledger asks whether the story was worth following. It asks only whether the sitting ended in a sale, and the sitting has no way to answer. Both are watching the same glass, and each is reading a different medium on it.

— Marshall McLuhan

stories.headline: Proof Is Not the Sale
stories.dek: A pixel can count what sold. It cannot make anything sell.
stories.body:
Netflix this month cut its 2026 advertising forecast to $2.7 billion from roughly $3 billion, blaming partner integrations that came more slowly than planned. The trade press treats this as a measurement story. It is a selling story. Money does not leave a medium because it has stopped showing programmes. It leaves because the advertiser cannot see what the advertising did, and the medium has been slow to show its work.

When I wrote for Hathaway, I did not know whether the eyepatch would work. I found out by counting shirts sold, and the copy that sold them told the reader something true about the shirt. A conversion pixel is a fine counting device. It cannot write the copy. Comscore's first score report says streaming holds 22 per cent of measured TV ad exposure time, and YouTube takes 44 per cent of that. Most of the screen's time still belongs to people who have not been asked to buy anything. The audience you can count is not always the audience you can persuade.

So the order of work is fixed. Build the advertisement that sells first. Then install the pixel and count the result, because a measurement tells you whether you were right; it does not make you right. Never the other way round. Stop buying television as though the dashboard were the product, and stop writing copy for the dashboard. Write it for the person on the sofa, who has never heard of a conversion event and has every right to switch channels.

— David Ogilvy

what_to_watch: Netflix's in-DSP measurement for Trade Desk buyers has no date; watch whether the November audience launch brings it, and whether the 2026 forecast cut slows partner integrations.
